commit.message:
style: replace all em dashes with hyphens

Swap every em dash (U+2014) for an ASCII hyphen across docs, skills, evals,
and the workflow file so text renders identically on every terminal/editor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

final polish: beginner clarity nits from the last review pass

- README: clarify YOUR-USERNAME is your fork's username; add an `ls .claude/skills`
  confirm step so a failed copy is caught before "review this PRD" silently no-ops.
- prd-reviewer output table header matches the check title verbatim.
- .gitignore spreadsheet section gets the same "broad by design, git add -f to keep
  a template" inline guidance the secrets/PII sections already have.
- competitor-scan / feedback-synthesizer: clarify the ignore protection keys off the
  dated filename, not the folder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

remove stray .aws-credentials-test; tighten .aws glob; doc nits

- A 0-byte .aws-credentials-test (a stray a grading pass touched in the working
  tree, swept in by an earlier `git add -A`) was tracked at root — exactly the
  kind of credential-named file this repo teaches you NOT to commit. Removed it,
  and added `.aws*` so flat AWS-credential files are caught going forward (the
  rule was directory-only). Committing with explicit paths now, not `git add -A`.
- autoresearch/README: "seed plus five optimization rounds" (last "six rounds"
  instance).
- Quick Start: tell a terminal-novice how to open a terminal and where the clone
  lands before the first command.
- calendar eval dated 2026-04-10 to match the decision that co-references it
  (was 04-13, a 3-day forward-reference); clarified each input scores out of 3
  or 4 since criteria 3-4 are conditional.
- Expanded PII on first use in the README.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

harden: cloud-cred gitignore, deterministic PRE-PRD, generative-skill examples

- .gitignore now ignores the most-leaked cloud/infra credential files
  (.aws/, kubeconfig, .kube/config, .docker/config.json,
  application_default_credentials.json). Verified shipped source unaffected.
- prd-reviewer PRE-PRD trigger was non-deterministic: a doc titled "PRD" with
  few sections could slip to PRE-PRD and dodge a NOT READY. Now a "PRD"/"spec"
  title is always held to the full standard; PRE-PRD needs a draft/brief title
  AND <=2 core sections.
- competitor-scan and feedback-synthesizer now ship a good-vs-bad output sample,
  satisfying CONTRIBUTING's examples bar (reworded to fit generative skills, not
  just checker skills).
- good-vs-bad-commits.md now scopes the autoresearch log command to the prompt
  file (matches README) so the listed rounds actually match the output.
- README: "seed plus five rounds" (not "six rounds"), a harmless-CRLF note for
  Windows, PowerShell Copy-Item -Force + re-run hint, and a mkdir step for
  adding a skill in the Exercise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs/ci: document .github, scope autoresearch log, gitleaks org note, polish

- README "What's Inside" now lists the .github/ folder (PR template, CODEOWNERS,
  gitleaks workflow) it had been shipping undocumented.
- Workflow 3 / autoresearch README now scope `git log` to launch-announcement-
  writer.md, so the run shows exactly the six rounds instead of interleaving
  later doc edits to the folder.
- gitleaks.yml: documented that org-owned forks need a free GITLEAKS_LICENSE
  secret (it was billed as "the real safety net" but fails silently in orgs)
  and wired the env var. CONTRIBUTING explains CODEOWNERS + branch protection.
- CLAUDE.md template now opens with a comment flagging the [BRACKETED] values
  as fill-ins (Claude loads it every session).
- Skills: the "git-ignored by default" guarantee is now tied to keeping the
  dated filename, since the ignore rule keys off the date.
- eval how-to template gains Last reviewed + a revision-log stub to match the
  worked evals; Step 5 reframed as "20+ inputs" to fit the 25-input run.
- sample PRD comment now lists every failing check, not just check 4.
- .gitignore catches loose db/sqlite data exports; PM-OS clone path placeholder
  reads YOUR-CLONE-PATH.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

harden: gitignore balance, .github governance, temporal + jargon

- .gitignore over-corrected last round (broad substrings swallowed legit docs
  like interview-prep.md, token-economy-prd.md, and even an example skill).
  Re-anchored: secrets scoped to real credential FILE forms (*.json/*.yaml/keys),
  PII scoped to the DATED outputs the skills emit and to research dirs. Verified
  both directions with git check-ignore — legit docs commit, real secrets/PII don't.
- Shipped the governance the docs prescribe: .github/workflows/gitleaks.yml
  (secret scanning on push/PR), a sample CODEOWNERS, and a PR template that
  auto-fills the Exercise submission.
- Fixed temporal impossibilities a sharp reader hits: "sustained 3 weeks" ->
  "across 3 runs" (was only 8 days after baseline); renamed the decision to
  2026-04-10 so it predates the eval that cites it (no forward reference);
  updated all four references.
- Jake Torres was both Calendar PM and Engineer lead across files — gave the
  eng lead a distinct name (Dana Wu).
- README: documented the `less` pager exit (press q) — the most common
  first-command trap; expanded PRD/PR/PII on first use; reworded the mobile
  callout to stop overstating the GitHub app; clarified the Claude-prompt vs
  shell boundary and the Windows "not recognized" PATH case.
- autoresearch: glossed the "Karpathy loop" and linked the Autoresearch Guide.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: gitignore breadth, PRD check-1 clarity, cross-links, jargon, mobile

- .gitignore: catch prefixed service-account keys (*service-account*.json,
  *service_account*.json), non-dotfile env files (*.env), and single-file PII
  (*transcript*, *interview*, *-raw.*) — the directory-only forms missed the
  loose files a PM actually creates. Verified with git check-ignore.
- prd-reviewer Check 1 was strict (demanded a number+timeframe) while its title
  said only "testable", making it ambiguous on the sample PRD. Scoped Check 1 to
  a testable direction + measurable effect; the numeric threshold is Check 2's
  job. Sample PRD now cleanly passes Check 1 and fails Check 4 as documented.
- Made the decision-log's "Referenced by" claim true: added back-links from the
  calendar eval and the project CLAUDE.md to decisions/.
- Both research skills now warn their output filename is git-ignored (PII) with
  the `git add -f` escape hatch.
- README: edit-the-source-not-the-copy warning, clone "already exists" and push
  403 troubleshooting, Windows note on the PM-OS block, a "reading on your phone"
  callout, and a .gitignore-is-tuned caveat.
- Expanded jargon for ESL/beginners (GA, dogfood, CRUD -> settings toggle).
- run-log start time set to the overnight window the autoresearch commits run in.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

align content dates with commit dates after history re-date

History was re-dated to be strictly monotonic in topological order (the
backdated story commits had read as time-travel). That left a few in-file
dates (eval review dates, the autoresearch run start) sitting after their
own commits. Pulled them back so the revision logs and run-log match when
the work actually landed in git — no more doc-vs-history date drift.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

harden: secrets coverage, sample PRD, decision log, eval N/A rule

Completeness + correctness pass on the finer findings:
- .gitignore SECRETS block now covers the common real-world cases (id_rsa,
  credentials.json, *token*, service-account*.json, .npmrc, *.p12, ...) so the
  "keeps secrets out" promise actually holds; verified with git check-ignore.
  Rewrote the PII comment to match real behavior and narrowed the negations to
  shipped source only, so a PII-named file dropped into skills/ or evals/ is
  still caught.
- Added examples/sample-prd.md (deliberately incomplete) so prd-reviewer has
  something to run against; Quick Start now points at it.
- Added decisions/ with a worked decision-log entry — the decision guide
  referenced the folder but it never shipped. Ties the calendar eval, project
  CLAUDE.md, and sample PRD together.
- calendar eval: criteria 3 and 4 are conditional on request type; added the
  N/A scoring rule so the eval isn't self-contradictory.
- prd-reviewer: gave PRE-PRD an objective trigger (titled brief, or <=2 of 5
  core sections) so it can't flip a verdict on undefined judgment.
- filled CLAUDE.md example: caution not to put real colleague names/notes in a
  public/forked repo.
- README: "v1->v7 plus later fixes" (matches the 10-commit log), claude exit +
  command-not-found help, .gitattributes in the tree, complete Coming-From-PM-OS
  flow (branch -M main, remote add, push), per-file workflow pointer, and the
  title link reads "Product Growth newsletter" instead of promising a post.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs/skills: beginner commit step, prune payoff, skill edge cases

- README: the Exercise's commit step now spells out `git add` + `git commit`
  + a `git log` verify line (it was the one place a beginner acts alone and
  got no command). Skill activation promoted from an optional-sounding tip to
  a required numbered step. Added a Windows/Git Bash note at Quick Start, and
  made the PM-OS clone path concrete instead of /path/to/this-repo.
- The CLAUDE.md prune commit said it "moved" the calendar rule to the project
  CLAUDE.md — so actually put it there. The prune lesson now pays off.
- prd-reviewer: reconciled the pre-PRD edge case with the missing=FAIL rule
  (pre-PRD overrides the verdict), and clarified the score denominator is 5
  for non-AI PRDs (checks 6-7 excluded, not failed).
- feedback-synthesizer: Quote Bank is now "up to 15-20, fewer is fine, never
  pad" so it stops fighting the never-invent rule on small inputs.
- .gitignore: PII globs now catch undated outputs too; negations still keep
  everything under skills/ and evals/ committable (re-verified).
- run-log / good-vs-bad / CONTRIBUTING: describe round 3 as the two changes
  it actually made (worked example + lead-with-audience rule).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix self-contradictory verdict rubric and remaining doc accuracy nits

- prd-reviewer verdict bands overlapped: a PRD failing only check 1/2/4
  matched both NEEDS WORK and NOT READY. Rewrote as first-match-wins,
  load-bearing-first, so exactly one verdict applies.
- Filled in calendar-integration eval (owner/dates) so it reads as a worked
  example like its sibling, not a half-template.
- good-vs-bad-commits.md and CONTRIBUTING.md listed "Good" commits that don't
  exist next to a "run git log to confirm" framing. Swapped both fictional
  lines for real commits from this repo's history.
- project-level example now states test-events.json must be synthetic; real
  attendee data is PII and belongs in the git-ignored data/exports/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

README: fix history-distance claim, tree drift, and two link issues

- Workflow 2 said the calendar rule is pruned "two commits later"; it's the
  very next commit. A beginner running `git log -p -- CLAUDE.md` sees the
  prune immediately, so the number contradicted the lesson. Fixed.
- "What's Inside" tree omitted calendar-integration-criteria.md and
  autoresearch/README.md, both of which ship. Added them.
- Dropped the specific "/upgrade-to-team-os" command name (not documented in
  the linked article) for the neutral "Team OS upgrade flow".
- Claude Code install link now points at code.claude.com/docs (the old URL
  301-redirected). Noted the activation copy is git-ignored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

gitignore: stop committing duplicate skills; anchor PII globs to source

Two footguns a persona hit by following the README in order:
- .claude/skills/ wasn't ignored, so activating a skill (copy into
  .claude/skills/) and then running the Exercise's `git add` committed a
  second, drifting copy of every skill. Now ignored — skills/ stays the one
  source of truth.
- The research-output globs (competitor-*.md, feedback-synthesis-*.md) were
  unanchored and silently swallowed files anywhere, including inside
  skills/competitor-scan/. Anchored to the DATED form the skills actually emit
  and added `!skills/**` / `!evals/**` so the repo's own source can never
  disappear from `git status`. Verified with git check-ignore.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

harden gitignore for PII, add gitattributes, fix Windows paths

- .gitignore now covers the PII-bearing outputs the skills generate
  (feedback-synthesis-*.md, competitor-*.md, interviews/, *transcript*),
  with a note on how to force-add a sanitized one. The repo markets itself
  as secrets-safe; a forker shouldn't be one `git add .` away from committing
  a transcript full of customer names.
- Added .gitattributes (text=auto eol=lf) so Windows checkouts don't spray
  CRLF noise into every diff.
- Decision guide: replaced brittle `git diff HEAD~20` with `git log -p`, added
  a PowerShell path variant, and reflected the now-demonstrated prune in the
  README workflow list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

CLAUDE.md: prune calendar PR rule (belongs in project CLAUDE.md)

Monthly pruning pass. The @jake-torres calendar rule is project-specific —
it only matters inside the calendar-integration repo, so it was burning
always-on global context for a sometimes-relevant instruction. Moved it to
that project's CLAUDE.md and removed it here. This is Workflow 2 in action:
`git log -p -- CLAUDE.md` shows the add and the prune.

Also swapped the brittle `git diff HEAD~20` in the footer for `git log -p`,
which works on a fresh fork instead of erroring with "ambiguous argument".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

CLAUDE.md: add calendar-integration PR rule

Tagging @jake-torres and linking PLANNING.md on every calendar PR — adding
it to the global file so I stop forgetting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

README: make the beginner cold-start actually work

Personas following the README literally hit three hard stops, plus a few
habit traps. Fixed all:
- Added a "Before you start" prereqs block: install Git (Git Bash on Windows),
  install Claude Code, and set git identity — the missing `git config` was
  aborting every first commit with "Author identity unknown".
- Default clone is now HTTPS (SSH-only was failing with "Permission denied
  (publickey)" for anyone without a key — i.e. most PMs); SSH kept as opt-in.
- The Exercise now branches (`git checkout -b`) before committing, instead of
  committing to main and then saying "open a PR" — matches the repo's own
  clean-history thesis. Points submitters at the right PR template.
- Added a note that skills load from .claude/skills/, with the copy/symlink
  command to activate them.
- "Coming From PM OS" now copies .gitignore in before `git add .` so secrets
  don't land in the first commit.
- Dropped the unqualified "5 minutes" claim that ignored setup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

evals: add calendar-integration criteria (fixes dangling ref) + expand acronyms

- examples/project-level-claude-md.md pointed at evals/calendar-integration-
  criteria.md, which didn't exist. Added it as a real second worked eval
  (4 binary criteria, baseline 0.72 -> target 0.85), so every referenced
  path in the repo now resolves.
- Spelled out acronyms ESL readers got stuck on: PAN (primary account number)
  and PMF (product-market fit).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

skills: use real activation (description, not triggers) + harden prd-reviewer

- All three skills used a non-standard `triggers:` front-matter key that
  Claude Code ignores — folded the trigger phrases into `description`, which
  is what activation actually keys on. A forker copying this pattern now gets
  skills that load.
- prd-reviewer (the flagship) lacked the Output Format / Edge Cases / Rules
  sections the other two skills and CONTRIBUTING.md require. Added them, plus
  an overall PASS/FAIL rollup.
- Fixed the stale eval example (3 criteria / 0.80 -> 4 criteria / 0.85) so it
  matches the repo's own worked eval.
- Resolved ambiguities personas hit: where the metric threshold must appear
  (checks 1 vs 2), how to decide a feature is AI-powered (gate on checks 6-7),
  and clarified this is a doc-completeness checklist, not a 3-6 eval function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix every doc-vs-git-history contradiction

The repo's whole thesis is "the docs mirror the git log." Several didn't:
- autoresearch/README inline log had round 5 inverted (showed 90->82; real
  commit is 82->90, restored best) and dropped round 4's score suffix. The
  one artifact whose point is "the log IS the lesson" misquoted the log.
  Replaced with a hash-free block that matches the messages verbatim, plus
  a `git log -p` command so it can't drift again.
- good-vs-bad-commits.md and CONTRIBUTING cited a "CTA example" round-3 commit
  that never existed (real: "before/after example"), mislabeled round 4 as the
  revert, and used Unicode arrows where git uses ASCII. Now mirror real commits.
- filled CLAUDE.md example claimed "34 lines" (it's 46); dropped the false
  count and added copy guidance.
- strengthened run-log round-4 rationale so the score drop is mechanically sound.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

README: document autoresearch/ folder, LICENSE, and live git histories

Reflect the new autoresearch sample run and MIT LICENSE in the file tree,
and point the four-workflow commands at the real paths so a forker can
run each one and see actual history.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

round 5 - revert word-count cap (82% -> 90%, restored best)

Loop reverted round 4 automatically: the prior commit's score was lower
than round 3, so the change loses. Back to the 90% prompt. Net effect of
rounds 1-5: 41% -> 90%.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

round 4 - cap at 80 words [EXPERIMENT] (score: 90% -> 82%)

Hypothesis: shorter announcements read better. Result: the 80-word cap
forced the model to drop the concrete numbers criterion 1 rewards, so
the score fell. Keeping the commit so the failed approach is on record;
round 5 reverts it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

round 3 - add worked example + lead-with-audience rule (score: 79% -> 90%)

Two prompt changes drove 79% -> 90% this round: a worked before/after
example, and a rule to lead with who the feature is for and what they can
now do (targets eval criterion 3). Bundled in one commit, so the log can't
split the credit between them -- a reminder to change one thing per round
when you want clean attribution.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

round 2 - ban buzzword list (score: 68% -> 79%)

Buzzwords were the cheap way to fake enthusiasm without saying anything.
Banning them forces specifics and lifts criterion 2 across the board.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

round 1 - require concrete numbers (score: 41% -> 68%)

Biggest single lever in the run. Forcing one concrete number kills the
vague-excitement failure mode that tanked the baseline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

autoresearch: seed launch-announcement-writer v0 (score: 41%)

Baseline prompt is deliberately vague ("make it exciting"). Scores 41%
against the 4-criterion eval. This is the starting point the overnight
loop optimizes from — the seed row in run-log.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

evals: raise target 0.80 -> 0.85, add revision log table

Prompt fix for the PII criterion landed; the chatbot has held 0.86 for
three weeks, so 0.85 is the new rollout floor. Added a dated revision-log
table so the eval-versioning workflow is legible from the file itself,
not just the git history.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

evals: add criterion 4 - never echo full card/account numbers

Security review found a transcript where the bot repeated a full PAN
back to the user. Adding a hard-fail criterion so the eval catches this
class of leak going forward. This is a raised bar, not a regression —
expect the next scored run to dip until the prompt is updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

evals: record 0.71 baseline from first 20-question run

First scored run against last week's support logs came in at 0.71,
below the 0.80 target. Logging the number and run date so future
score drops can be diagnosed (criteria moved vs. model regressed).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

add MIT LICENSE and replace placeholder links with live URLs

- README claimed MIT but shipped no LICENSE file; add it (fixes fork/reuse ambiguity)
- Replace dead (link-newsletter)/(link-internal-*) placeholders across README,
  decision guide, and eval guide with real news.aakashg.com / aibyaakash.com URLs
- Dead links are the first thing a forker hits; none remain
